points.description: Function prototype (declaration) gives the function signature: name, return type and parameter types, without the body.
points.partial_credit: 2 marks if only vaguely stated (e.g. 'declares the function') or the signature is given with a wrong or missing element.

points.description: Function definition contains the actual body (implementation/code) of the function.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both sides of the contrast: the prototype is the signature (name, return type, parameter types) and the definition contains the function body. Different wording is fine, and 'declaration' for prototype is accepted. Give part marks for a vague or half-stated prototype idea. Give nothing for answers that only talk about calling or using functions without stating the fact.
